text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Russian novelist ALEXANDER SOLZHENITSYN was born in 1918.
Australian entertainer REG LIVERMORE was born in 1938 in Sydney.

American singer, guitarist and songwriter with the group 'Bread' DAVID GATES was born in 1940. Hits included "Make It With You"(1970), "If"(1971), "Baby I'm-A Want You"(1971), "Everything I Own"(1972) and "The Guitar Man"(1972). In 1973 the group split up and reformed briefly in 1976 to have a hit with "Lost Without Your Love". DAVID had modest success as a solo artist with "Goodbye Girl"(1977).

US pop and country singer BRENDA LEE (BRENDA MAE TARPLEY) was born in 1944. At the age of 12 she had a recording contract and was successful shortly afterwards with hits such as "Sweet Nothin's"(1959), "I'm Sorry"(1960), "I Want To Be Wanted"(1960), "Break It To Me Gently"(1962) and "Losing You"(1963).

One of the JACKSON brothers, JERMAINE JACKSON, was born in 1954. He started with his brothers in the 'JACKSON Five', which was formed in 1967. He was the first of the clan to attempt a solo career. Hits included "Daddy's Home"(1972), "Let's Get Serious"(1980), "Do What You Do"(1984) and with PIA ZADORA "When The Rain Begins To Fall"(1984). JERMAINE joined his brothers once again in 1984 for the VICTORY album and the resulting tour. The lead singers were MICHAEL and JERMAINE.
US bassist and songwriter with the heavy metal band 'Motley Crue' NIKKI SIXX was born in 1958.
** EVENTS **
1769 : Venetian blinds were patented in London by EDWARD
BERAN.
1894 : The first motor show opened in Paris with nine
exhibitors.
1914 : In the Battle of the Falklands, all British ships
survived while four German cruisers were sunk.
1920 : Britain declared martial law in large parts of

Ireland in an attempt to contain the Irish Republican Army. Britain had more than 40-thousand troops and seven thousand of the hated Black and Tans (ex-soldier police) in search of IRA gunmen. Two weeks earlier the IRA had killed 14 experts who had been bought from the mainland to improve army intelligence.
1922 : At London's Old Bailey EDITH THOMPSON was
found jointly guilty with her lover, FREDERICK BYWATERS, of murdering her husband and sentenced to death.
1936 : King EDWARD the eighth broadcast his abdication

speech. Less than a year after his accession to the throne, the king ended months of speculation with a radio broadcast fron Windsor Castle. "I have found it impossible to carry the heavy burden of responsibility and to discharge my duties as king as I would wish to do without the help and support of the woman I love." He was referring to twice-divorced Mrs WALLACE SIMPSON. Immediately after the broadcast he boarded a Royal Navy destroyer, which took him to exile in France to join Mrs SIMPSON. The couple had met in 1933 and their affair began in 1934 and endured the protests of the royal family, the cabinet and the church. Prime Minister STANLEY BALDWIN told the King to choose between his throne and Mrs SIMPSON. He chose Mrs SIMPSON. EDWARD's younger brother became King GEORGE the sixth.
1941 : HITLER and MUSSOLINI declared war on the United
States.
1952 : Two British teenagers were found guilty of
murdering a London policeman. DEREK BENTLEY, 19, was sentenced to death, although it was his accomplice, CHRISTOPHER CRAIG, who fired the shot. CRAIG was only 16 and too young to hang.
1963 : FRANK SINATRA Junior was set free by kidnappers
after his father paid a ransom of 240,000 dollars.
1967 : The world's first supersonic airliner, the

Anglo-French Concorde, was rolled out of its hangar for the first time for public inspection. The aircraft was ordered by 16 airlines. The aircraft cruises at twice the speed of sound at about 2,170 kilometres per hour. It is 62 metres long and has a wing span of 26 metres. It made its first flight in 1969 and entered commercial service seven years later.
1976 : A poll revealed four out of ten Australians
supported the country becoming a Reupblic.
1987 : At Christie's auction house in London, CHARLIE
CHAPLIN's cane and bowler hat sold for 152,625 dollars and his boots fetched 71,225 dollars.
